sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent No.1.

Respondent No.2 who is served in the matter has remained unrepresented before this Court.
NC: 2024:KHC:45394 3. F.I.R. in Crime No.77/2024 was registered by Ramanagara Women Police Station, Ramanagar,
against the petitioner herein initially for the offences punishable under Sections 363 of IPC, on the basis of first information dated 11.06.2024 received from respondent No.2 herein who is the father of the victim girl.
During the course of the investigation petitioner herein and the victim were traced together.
The petitioner herein was arrested in case on 20.06.2024 and subsequently remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offence.
4. Bail application filed by the petitioner before the jurisdictional sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.758/2024 was rejected on 13.09.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that petitioner is a youngster, aged about 22 years and he has no criminal antecedents.
Material on record would go to NC: 2024:KHC:45394 show that petitioner and the victim girl were in love.

The victim girl had voluntarily accompanied the petitioner and had stayed with him till they were traced Mr Ravikumar vs State Of Karnataka on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54545322/
2 and brought back by the police.

sentences.text: Investigation in the case is completed and accordingly he prays to allow the petition.

6. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the bail petition and he submits that the victim girl is a minor and she had stated that the petitioner had sexual intercourse with her, therefore alleged offences get attracted against the accused.
He accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
7. First information was submitted by respondent No.2 who is the father of the victim girl, after the victim girl who had gone to school on 10.06.2024, had not returned home.
Efforts made by respondent No.2 to trace her had failed and therefore, on the next day, he had approached the police.
Since the first informant had suspected the hand of the petitioner, FIR was initially registered against the petitioner.
During the course of investigation petitioner herein and the victim girl were NC: 2024:KHC:45394 traced together.
The petitioner herein was arrested on 20.06.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
The victim was subjected to medical examination on 20.06.2024.
Before the Doctor who has medically examined the victim girl, she has stated that she was in love with the petitioner and they got married at Male Mahadeshwara Betta on 10.06.2024.
After that they stayed in the petitioner's uncle's house at Mandya for three days and had sexual intercourse.
8. Medical examination of the victim girl would go to show that she had not suffered any external injury on any parts of her body including the Genitals.
Statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of Cr.P.C was recorded before the Jurisdiction Magistrate on 24.06.2024.

The victim has stated that she was in love with the petitioner and after coming to know about the same, her father had abused her and had her parents intended to perform her marriage with another boy.

Therefore, she had left the house and gone along with the petitioner and got married NC: 2024:KHC:45394 at Mahadevshwara Betta on 10.06.2024, subsequently, they stayed together in petitioner's uncle's house for three days.
Thereafter they had gone to the petitioner's friend's house and stayed together.
She has stated that she had gone along with the petitioner to meet an Advocate and police came there and brought back to them to their village.
9. Undisputedly, petitioner has no criminal antecedents and he, is aged about 22 years.
His continued detention is likely to have adverse impact on his future prospects and career.
Allegation as against the petitioner is required to be proved in the full-pledged trial.
Investigation in the case is completed.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail is required to be answered affirmatively.

10. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.
